Messages.Author: Intimate apperal
Messages.Body:
This is just some generic input on some points which I have seen in
several points. It in no way represents official information.

Master - Out of Turn: In the rules, in the section entilted What You Can
Do On Your Turn, there is no mention of playing this type of card - this
leads one to believe that one cannot play a master out of turn when it is
their turn. This could explain why master out of turn cards are cards
used to react to other events in the game, or perhaps this is just a
coincidence.

Cross table bleeds: In the corrected rules, section 13.3.1 Whom may Block
Whom, it reads "Directed actions are noted on action cards with a (D) in
the card text and allow you to dirrect the action against ANY
methuselah." This text indicates that cross table bleeds are legal. I
have also found that they tend to preserve game balance( not that they
should or shouldn't, but in the games I've played, they do)

Clan Hosers - clan hosers only present a problem in a friendly play
setting, and should be dealt with in frienly ways - i.e. you put five
Letter From Vienna, I put in Five Malkavian Dementia, and I build my deck
specifically against yours, wow I win - that sure was fun - now can we stop
playing like babies and show some maturity. In a tournament setting,
clan hosers are essentially useless, except in their intended format( the
weakness of my malk deck is tremere rush -> Letter From Vienna ) If I am
at a tournament, and someone asks me what clan I play with, I will flat
out lie to them and say Gangrel(really Tremere). When Sara Cobler comes
out in my first transfer phase, I will look at him, laugh, and say "Looks
like some idiot wishes he(or she) wouldn't have put those ten Gangrel De
Evolutions in their deck, now doesn't it, shmuck"

Messages.Author: Owen Reynolds
Messages.Body:
More and more people seem to feel the first draft of the rules was
the better one. Master OOT's were obviously intended at first to be
playable on your turn (played whenever applicable in lieu of your next
master phase.) The question is whether someone decided to change that
in the second set of rules or they just "dumbed it down" and ended up
saying something other than they intended.
If you look at the entire section describing master cards, it's
all very badly written. I played around and rewrote it (took 15 minutes)
to be easier to read, to explain more and to be shorter.
I wouldn't be surprised if someone were to show both sets of rules
to the design team and they'd look at them and say, "you're right -- they
can be used on your turn. Sorry."

>Allowing OOTM to be played during your current turn makes several of them
>unbabancing, to say the least. Surprisingly enough, this is one of the
>things that almost everyone who has played a significant amount of Jyhad
>eventually agrees on.

So, don't allow them to be played on your turn. Major Boon (or
whatever) shouldn't be playable on one of your bleeds, so let the
card say that. I doubt anyone who allows OOTs on your turn would allow
it, anyway. How is saving you from my bleed doing you a favor?

Does allowing Sudden Reversal or Frenzy to be played on your turn
cause any serious problems?

Sorry to pick on your post, Shane, but I just came across this, and I'm
tired of people hiding behind the "English" of an idiomatic expression:

Webster's III New Riverside University Dictionary (1984):
Turn:
- out of turn: 1. Not in the proper sequence or order.

So, it IS out-of-phase, or whatever else you want to call it, and this is
how the original rules read. (Just because they allow you to play the
things when is _is_not_your_turn_ [13.1], doesn't mean you can't play them
when it _is_ your turn.)

>Allowing OOTM to be played during your current turn makes several of them
>unbabancing, to say the least. Surprisingly enough, this is one of the
>things that almost everyone who has played a significant amount of Jyhad
>eventually agrees on.

The (mis-)errata is the only thing turning what used to be a balanced
effect (SR of an SR, Frenzy when you are blocked, etc.) into an unbalanced
one ("grossly unbalancing" is probably a little extreme).
Even Major Boon is not unbalanced, IMO. Take a bleed for your Prey?
That's border-line insane (until you happen to get a Malk Predator, of
course, then it's just like any other time you could officially play the
*$!@ card.)

And I've played a few games with the mis-errata to know that it unbalances
the games around here.

Just so you can sleep easy knowing that there is not a consensus to be had
on the net :-).

Personally, it may just be the way that I view the 'game world', but I
have a problem with a Meth1 playing a Master, Meth2 SRing it, and Meth1
SRing the SR.

See, I view it this way: Meth1 is expending all of the energy/time he has
to pull off this effect (whatever it may be). Meth2, having gotten wind
of it, puts his future plans on hold and expends all his energy at
stopping this effect. This exhausts him for a while (uses his next
Master Phase).

There simply _is_ no more time/energy for Meth1 to use in countering the
counter - his plans are in motion and require his constant attention.
Thus, he cannot send his own forces out to counter the destabiling forces
sent by Meth2.

I realize that this world=view may not work for everyone, but it works
for me, and I like the official' way of playing it. Anyone who doesn't
care to counter with how they justify it in _their_ world view?

"Turn" is a specifically defined term within the game.
Therefore the phrase "Out of turn" is ambiguous, since we cannot be sure
which definition of "turn" is being used in the phrase. If it is the
'usual' definition, then "out of sequence" is synonymous with "out of
turn," but if the word "turn" within the phrase indicates the
game-specific definition of the word, then "out of sequence" is no
longer a synonom, and "out of turn" specifically means "not on your
turn."
Neither side can know which definition of "turn" is being used
on the cards, and thus, the argument is a stalemate.
If you wish to keep going, feel free, but realize that what you
are debating is which definition of "turn" is being used in the phrase.

To a "correct English speaker," the term is ambiguous.
